newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli court asked to fine striking bank workers.
newsitem.headline: Israeli court asked to fine striking bank workers.

text.p: Israel's attorney-general asked the High Court on Thursday to impose fines on union leaders as bank employees prepared to strike for the third Friday in a row.

Workers at Israel's major banks, demanding a five-day work week, have been conducting a one-day-a-week strike despite a court decision ordering them to work during at least half the banks' opening hours.
Employees violated the court order last week, forcing banks to remain closed all day.

"Violation of the court order is a severe blow to the rule of law...and to (bank) customers," said the attorney-general's office in a petition requesting that judges issue contempt of court orders against strike leaders.
Union officials say management has been bargaining in bad faith, prompting bank workers to continue their sanctions.
"Our position is that the court order should be honoured but you can assume workers will strike for the whole day," said Zion Shema, the head of the Histadrut labour federation's bank workers union.
Shema said the banks had agreed to move to a five-day work week but were refusing to implement the agreement. Israeli banks operate Sunday through Thursday and for a half day on Friday.

Bank officials have said agreements to coordinate a move to a five-day week were rejected by Israel's anti-trust authorities, which ruled the banks could not make a collective decision to stop providing service on Friday.
The Friday strikes have affected all of Israel's major banks. Banks at border crossings and direct banking services have remained open, along with some of the smaller banks.
